panels.rationale: Single photograph of infant diaper showing orange crystalline sediment; caption explicitly attributes it to hyperuricosuria as key early manifestation of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome in case 1, 4-month-old baby, matching vocabulary term orange crystalluria.
panels.attribution_text: Fang et al. Whole Exome Sequencing Facilitates Early Diagnosis of Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome: A Case Series.. Diagnostics (Basel, Switzerland) 2024. doi:10.3390/diagnostics14242809. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Orange-colored crystalline sediment in the diaper was noted when the baby (case 1) was 4 months old. The sediment is indicative of hyperuricosuria, a key early manifestation of LNS.
in_text_mentions: born at 39 weeks and 4 days with a birth weight of 3414 g. During a clinical evaluation, persistent hypotonia interspersed with episodes of spasticity, intermittent neck hyperextension, and poor head control were noted. In addition, he had mild hypotonia of the extremities, muscle strength graded at 4–5, brisk deep tendon reflexes (+++), and questionable bilateral ankle clonus. His mother noticed orange-colored crystalline sediment in his diaper when he was 4 months old (Figure 1). Developmentally, he showed significant motor delays, being unable to sit or stand independently by 1 year of age.

plate_findings.evidence: (a–c) Tophus of the left index finger and wrist

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 6 panels (A, B, C, D, E, F). A: Intraoperative clinical photo of finger tophus debridement in case report titled Late diagnosis of Lesch-Nyhan disease with tophi burst; caption attributes to tophus. B: Clinical photo of finger tophus with bleeding/debridement in Lesch-Nyhan case with end-stage renal disease and tophi burst. C: Open wrist surgical exploration revealing tophi of several joints per in-text; captioned as tophus of wrist. D: Clinical photo of burst ankle tophus with discharging lesion in Lesch-Nyhan disease case. E: Intraoperative ankle exploration showing tophaceous tissue, part of burst ankle tophus series. F: Ex vivo gross photo of excised tophaceous stones/crystals from Lesch-Nyhan patient debridement; direct visualization of gouty tophi.
panels.attribution_text: Ambarsari et al. Late diagnosis of Lesch-Nyhan disease complicated with end-stage renal disease and tophi burst: a case report.. Renal failure 2020. doi:10.1080/0886022x.2020.1713805. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: (a–c) Tophus of the left index finger and wrist. (d–f) Tophus of the left ankle burst and discharged stones and crystals.
in_text_mentions: Chest radiography showed thoracic scoliosis (Figure 3(a)). Arthrography or joint X-ray of the left hand and ankle showed revealed the presence of tissue masses (Figure 3(b–d)). After the lump on the left ankle burst, debridement and exploration sessions were performed in the left wrist and ankle, which revealed tophi of several joints (Figure 4(a–f)). Along with the debridement and exploration procedures, bone biopsy results confirmed juvenile gouty arthritis (Figure 5(a–c)).

Single lump was seen on the antihelix of the earlobe (Figure 2(c)), along with multiple lumps on his extremities (Figure 2(d,e)) and larger lumps similar to abscesses on his left hand and ankle (Figure 2(f)). panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: Panel-specific caption states urate crystals on bone biopsy; in-text states biopsy confirmed juvenile gouty arthritis in Lesch-Nyhan disease case with tophi burst, supporting gouty tophi attribution. b: Panel-specific caption states urate crystals on bone biopsy; in-text states biopsy confirmed juvenile gouty arthritis in Lesch-Nyhan disease case with tophi burst, supporting gouty tophi attribution. c: Panel c captioned as demineralization as part of same bone biopsy figure confirming juvenile gouty arthritis in Lesch-Nyhan disease with tophi; interpreted as tophaceous bone involvement.

in_text_mentions: Chest radiography showed thoracic scoliosis (Figure 3(a)). Arthrography or joint X-ray of the left hand and ankle showed revealed the presence of tissue masses (Figure 3(b–d)). After the lump on the left ankle burst, debridement and exploration sessions were performed in the left wrist and ankle, which revealed tophi of several joints (Figure 4(a–f)). Along with the debridement and exploration procedures, bone biopsy results confirmed juvenile gouty arthritis (Figure 5(a–c)).

B: Panel B is extraoral clinical photo showing nasal ulcer with loss of columella from self-mutilation plus lip sucking/biting and saliva, in Lesch-Nyhan case report. Lip biting vocabulary finding supported by caption; nasal self-injury recorded as proposed finding.
